verses.verse:
छन्दों बद्धो यथा वाक्यः सर्वस्मै रोचते खलु।
ताले बद्धस्तथा रागों गायकस्य धनं महत्।१२९।
verses.text: Just as a sentence bound in metre pleases everyone, so a rāga bound in tāla is the singer's great wealth.

commentary.text: That is, when a sentence is endowed with qualities such as figures of speech (alaṅkāra), it is called prose poetry (gadya kāvya), which pleases only poets. But when that same sentence is bound into a beautiful chanda (metre), it becomes pleasing to all people. These two kinds can be seen in all things of the world: loose tea and packed tea, loose cloth and stitched clothes, plain talk and talk steeped in rasa (aesthetic flavour), a naked creature and a creature clothed, and so on. In every field each has its own importance. The essence of this is that -
